We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid (alkene). (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (or amine). Then break alkene to give aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retrosynthesis: the unsaturated acid fragment (the part /C=C/C(=O)N...) came from aldehyde + malonic acid. So we can disconnect the double bond to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2?) Wait the unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via double bond: /C=C/C(=O)N... The α,β-unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring: the double bond conjugated to aromatic ring. In Doebner, aldehyde (aryl) + malonic acid -> aryl-CH=CH-CO2H (cinnamic acid). So our fragment is c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N...)cc2. So the aryl ring with the unsaturated acid side chain is a cinnamic acid derivative. So retrosynthesis: break to aryl aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then the amide formation: the carboxylic acid (cinnamic acid) reacts with an amine (aniline c3ccccc3N) to give amide. So we need to break amide to give cinnamic acid and aniline.

Finally sulfonamide formation: the sulfonamide linking the first phenyl (with methyl) to the second phenyl (c2...). So break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). Actually sulfonamide formation forward: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl? Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(...). The sulfonyl group attached to the first phenyl via N. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be ClSO2-c2ccc(...). So we need to generate that from the second phenyl (the one bearing the cinnamic acid). So we can propose sulfonyl chloride derived from that phenyl.

Thus overall route:

Target -> (1) disconnect amide: give cinnamic acid (with sulfonyl phenyl attached) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). (2) disconnect alkene: give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid. (3) disconnect sulfonamide: give sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-c2ccc(...)) and aniline (the methyl phenyl). Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl (c2...). So after step 2 we have the aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2). To get sulfonyl chloride, we need to convert that aromatic ring to sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl). That is a functional group transformation not in guidance but we can treat as separate step: sulfonyl chloride formation from aryl (maybe via chlorosulfonation). But we only have 3 steps total, as per task. The three steps are: amide formation, Doebner modification, sulfonamide formation. So the sulfonyl chloride is considered as a starting material (available). So retrosynthesis: target -> amide disconnection -> cinnamic acid + aniline. Cinnamic acid derived from Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid. Aldehyde derived from sulfonyl chloride? Actually the aldehyde is the same aromatic ring that later becomes sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the same aromatic ring that also bears the cinnamic acid side chain. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the same aromatic ring but with sulfonyl chloride instead of sulfonamide. So we need to have sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic ring that also has the aldehyde? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the aromatic ring at the position where the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches. In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (methyl phenyl). The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl (c2...). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be ClSO2-c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (i.e., sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic ring that also has aldehyde). That seems plausible: we can have sulfonyl chloride on aromatic ring, then sulfonamide formation with the first aniline (methyl phenyl amine). So the sulfonyl chloride is a starting material.

Thus retrosynthetic steps:

Step 1 (retro): break amide -> cinnamic acid (with sulfonyl chloride attached) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). Wait the amide is between the cinnamic acid carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide precursor is the cinnamic acid (with sulfonyl chloride) and aniline.

Step 2 (retro): break alkene -> aldehyde (ClSO2-c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid.

Step 3 (retro): break sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + aniline (the methyl phenyl amine, i.e., p-toluidine). Actually the sulfonamide formation step is forward: p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide linking to second phenyl. So retro: sulfonamide -> p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1), sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-c2ccc(CHO)cc2), malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH), aniline (c3ccccc3N) (but note aniline is also a product of amide formation; we already have aniline as separate). Actually the amide formation uses aniline as nucleophile; the sulfonamide formation uses p-toluidine. So we have two different amines.

Thus we need to propose route with three reactions:

1. Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CHO) -> sulfonamide intermediate (p-tolyl-NH-SO2-Ph-CHO). (But the sulfonyl chloride also has aldehyde; that's okay.)

2. Doebner modification: the aldehyde on that intermediate reacts with malonic acid to give the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) attached to sulfonyl phenyl. So product is sulfonyl phenyl with cinnamic acid side chain.

3. Amide formation: the cinnamic acid reacts with aniline to give the final amide.

Thus we need to find templates for each step.

We need to retrieve template IDs for each transformation.

We can search for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Use functional_groups_broken: ["carboxylic acid"]? Actually broken is aliphatic carboxylic acid. Let's search.
